examples.english: Satsuma-age is a versatile ingredient that can be used in both simmered and stir-fried dishes.

notes:
さつま{揚|あ}げ is a popular fried fish cake originating from Kagoshima ({薩摩|さつま}) in southern Japan.

WRITING:
- {薩摩|さつま} (old name for Kagoshima) + {揚|あ}げ (fried)
- Can be written as {薩摩揚|さつまあ}げ but usually in hiragana

INGREDIENTS:
- Made from ⟦すり{身|み}→すり身：08774_surimi⟧ (fish paste/surimi)
- Often mixed with vegetables like ⟦{牛蒡|ごぼう}→牛蒡：13484_gobou⟧, ⟦{人参|にんじん}→人参：05185_ninjin⟧
- Some varieties contain cheese, corn, or other fillings

REGIONAL NAMES:
- Called てんぷら in western Japan
- Called ⟦{揚|あ}げかまぼこ→揚げかまぼこ：26254_agekamaboko⟧ in some regions
- In Kagoshima, called つけあげ

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦おでん→おでん：14727_oden⟧ (oden hot pot)
- ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧ (simmered dishes)
- ⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧ (stir-fries)
- ⟦そのまま→そのまま：03322_sonomama⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ (eaten as is, often grilled)

ETYMOLOGY:
- Said to be influenced by Chinese/Ryukyuan cuisine
- Became popular from Kagoshima region

RELATED FOODS:
- ⟦かまぼこ→かまぼこ：10307_kamaboko⟧ (fish cake - not fried)
- ⟦ちくわ→ちくわ：07479_chikuwa⟧ (tube-shaped fish cake)
- ⟦はんぺん→はんぺん：21733_hanpen⟧ (white fish cake)
